title: Steve Jobs on A players, amplification, education and perseverance (Smithsonian, 1995)
summary: In a 1995 Smithsonian oral history, Jobs explains why he obsessed over only hiring A players, how the Macintosh team amplified their values a million to one, and why technology and art are not separate. He also argues people matter more than computers in education, and that perseverance and passion separate successful entrepreneurs.

principles.text: Keep the organization to A players only; the best people are worth many times the average.
principles.quote: That's what I consider one of the few things I actually can contribute individually--to to really try to instill in the organization the goal of only having 'A' players.

principles.text: In software the gap between best and worst is huge, so always go after the best people in the world.
principles.quote: Therefore, I have found, not just in software, but in everything I've done it really pays to go after the best people in the world.

principles.text: The best work happens where technical excellence and humanistic values meet; artists and engineers pursue the same goal.
principles.quote: The things I'm most proud about at Apple is where the technical and the humanistic came together

principles.text: A small team can amplify its values enormously; steer a product early because small changes compound.
principles.quote: What's interesting is that if you change the course of a vector near its origin, by time it gets a few miles out its course is radically different.

principles.text: Companies decline when profit and greed replace the product values that built them.
principles.quote: What ruined Apple wasn't growth. What ruined Apple was values.

principles.text: Be passionate about the problem; perseverance is half of what separates successful entrepreneurs.
principles.quote: I'm convinced that about half of what separates the successful entrepreneurs from the non-successful ones is pure perseverance.
